selection.reason: In this conditional stress-test model, Combined Damage Focus deploys all five available crews across specialized and general tasks to achieve multi-metric gains without increasing building isolation. Compared to No Action Control across the three capacity sensitivity cases (low, central, high), it avoids a mean of 3.33 flooded entrances (range 2 to 4), 400.18 m3 of interior water (range 213.40 to 513.14 m3), 0.33 failed trees (range 0 to 1), 0.14 unserved load hours (range 0.0 to 0.37), and 42.67 route hazard minutes (range 8.0 to 60.0). Meanwhile, damaged envelope area (mean 44,256.84 m2), partial collapses (mean 250.67), and isolated building minutes (mean 55,013.33) remain unchanged.
tradeoffs: Splitting the two general crews between entrance protection and securing loose roof objects reduces avoided flooded entrances from a mean of 5.33 (in Protect Entrances Only, which avoids 608.74 m3 of interior water) to 3.33 (avoiding 400.18 m3).

Omitting route closures avoids the access penalty seen in Close Routes Only, where closing 8 streets reduces route hazard exposure by a mean of 241.33 minutes (range 90.0 to 370.0) but harms access by increasing isolated building minutes by a mean of 177.33 (range 14.0 to 420.0).

Compared to Combined All Hazards, Combined Damage Focus sacrifices 81.33 mean avoided route hazard minutes (42.67 vs 124.0) in exchange for avoiding 1.00 more flooded entrance on average and 271.81 m3 more interior water, while avoiding the low-case interior water harm (-51.53 m3 avoided) triggered by tree pruning and flow interactions.

Arborist pruning on T249971 (with T13687 skipped due to the 120-minute travel and work window) avoids a mean of 0.33 failed trees, but in Prune Trees Only this alters local debris/flow interactions to increase mean interior water by 28.10 m3 (avoided -28.10 m3, range -87.65 to +3.35 m3).

Structural bracing on B201006.0164399 completes within the time limit but yields 0.0 avoided damaged envelope area and 0.0 avoided partial collapses across all three capacity sensitivity cases, as the target's failure state was not altered under this specific 20 m/s wind and 28 m/s gust scenario.
Scheduling 13 actions in Combined Damage Focus results in 11 completed and 2 skipped actions due to walking and return-to-staging time limits, leaving unfinished work uncredited.

hypothesis: Single-family advance preparation plans isolate specific hazard mitigations within crew and time constraints, while combined multi-discipline portfolios utilize all five specialized and general crews simultaneously to reduce roof/wall damage, entrance flooding, power loss, and route exposure, at the cost of increased route isolation from closures.

sources.name: DataSF building footprints
sources.basis: Mapped geometry and older measured height; structural condition is not recorded.

assumptions: Conditional stress test: mapped geometry is real; structural condition, load capacities, roof objects, entrance ratings and work durations are scenario inputs, not surveyed findings.
Three matched capacity cases (0.65, 1.0, 1.35) are sensitivity cases, not event probabilities. Same latent strengths and weather are reused for every plan.
Roof/wall assembly failure is modeled for buildings below 20 m. Whole high-rise stability, dynamic response, waves and foundation scour remain outside this model.
Wind loads use q=0.613 V² with directional coefficients. This is a simplified load model, not CFD validation. Tree dimensions use DBH-based allometry; tree condition is unobserved.

Tree overturning capacity is an explicit 35–55 m/s dry-anchorage sensitivity, with crown streamlining and wet-soil reduction. It is not a universal failure threshold or a calibration to SF trees; stem fracture is not resolved.

Only source-classified overhead lines can be struck by trees. PG&E feeder installation type is unknown. Building-to-feeder association is a nearest-route assumption, not a verified customer connection.
Substation equipment height and damage threshold are conditional inputs; no actual outage is asserted. Local islanded backup powers one modeled 10 kW load, not the public network.

Backup candidates assume a compatible pre-installed transfer connection. Bracing assumes an engineered four-anchor kit and access method. These prerequisites are scenario conditions, not facts in GIS.
Route exposure counts hazardous open street-link minutes, not people or injuries. Closures affect access and can worsen isolation. No casualty predictions or dollar-loss claims.
Five crews (two general, one arborist, one structural, one electrician); walking at 1.4 m/s on the street graph. Skills, finite kits, travel, work and return time are enforced before storm onset.
The preparation window is assumed accessible and calm; work requires owner access and approved methods before storm onset. It is not authorization or a real work order.
Up to 24 hypothetical 3 kg roof objects are allocated from the loose-debris slider inventory; the remainder is surface litter. Their locations are scenario placements, not observations.

source_types.demand: One modeled 10 kW load per building; not utility customer data
